name: ML365
synonyms: compound 35 of the bis-amide series (Flaherty 2014); probe report name ML365
identifier: PubChem CID 46785920 (name match; C22H20N2O3; 2-methoxy-N-[3-[(3-methylbenzoyl)amino]phenyl]benzamide, which fits the 3-methylphenyl plus 2-alkoxyphenyl bis-amide described in the source); not in the LEGEND compound catalogue (compound_identity.py: NOT_FOUND_BY_NAME) [V5: identifiers in tools.tsv are PubChem name matches (CID, formula, IUPAC name) without InChIKey and not compared with a structure drawn in a source; only ML365 is text-consistent with Table 2 of Flaherty 2014.]
target_composition: TASK-1 (KCNK3) homomer inhibitor; TASK-3 inhibited about 60-fold less
assay: (1) thallium-flux assay in CHO cells expressing TASK-1 or TASK-3, medium HBSS pH 7.4; (2) QPatch automated whole-cell, 14 NaCl 140 KCl 1 MgCl2 1.8 CaCl2 10 HEPES pH 7.4
relation: IC50 (inhibition); ratio TASK-3/TASK-1 100 (TF, 97.5 from the printed values) and 62 (QPatch)
selectivity_panel_measured: KCNQ2, hERG and Kir2.1 (each IC50 > 30 uM for the series unless noted); parental TASK-1 cells at 30 uM; TASK-3 (see value); hit rate under 0.5 percent in other PubChem assays (for the hit compound 3, not for 35)
not_tested: TREK-1, TREK-2, TRAAK, TASK-2, THIK, TWIK, TRESK and the TASK-1/TASK-3 heteromer: not in this paper; no pH other than 7.4
alternative_actions: ML365 inhibits TWIK2 (title-level hit in the Europe PMC string Q39, 2022, not opened); the series has a hERG IC50 of 12.4 uM for one other analog (not 35)
neuronal_evidence: Yang 2022: 10 nM had no effect on holding current or membrane resistance in adult rat DMV neurons (n = 5). O Donohoe 2018: 4-4000 nM raised [Ca2+]i in neonatal rat carotid body type-1 cells (non-saturating; not a neuron)
pH_dependence_of_tool: not tested: all potency assays at pH 7.4 only; a pH-dependent block cannot be excluded or confirmed from these sources
role_proposed: conditional (probe of TASK-1 over TASK-3 only; untested against TREK-1 and the heteromer)
locator: Table 4 and text (Flaherty); Fig 6B legend (Yang); Figure 7 (O Donohoe)

name: A1899
identifier: PubChem CID 9827303 (name match; C30H26F2N2O3; N-[(2,4-difluorophenyl)methyl]-2-[2-[[[2-(4-methoxyphenyl)acetyl]amino]methyl]phenyl]benzamide); structure not checked against an opened source; not in the LEGEND catalogue (NOT_FOUND_BY_NAME)
target_composition: TASK-1 (KCNK3) inhibitor, open-pore blocker; TASK-3 about 10-fold weaker (copied)
assay: Copied pair (Streit 2011 via O Donohoe): oocytes; measured here: HEK-293 cell-attached single-channel nPopen, 140 K+ pipette pH 7.4 at 37 C; native type-1 cells cell-attached, HCO3-/CO2 Tyrode pH 7.4, 36-37 C
value: copied IC50 35 (TASK-1) and 318 (TASK-3) nM; measured: 63.4 ± 7.7 percent inhibition of TASK-1 at 400 nM (n = 4); native type-1 cells 34 ± 7 percent at 400 nM (n = 8), above 60 percent at 4000 nM, no saturation
relation: IC50 (copied, ratio about 9); percent inhibition of nPopen (measured)
selectivity_panel_measured: not measured in the paper read: the O Donohoe study did not test A1899 on TASK-3; it reports no effect of 400 nM on the Ca2+ response to 30 mM K+ in type-1 cells (voltage-gated Ca2+ entry intact)
not_tested: TASK-3 and TASK-1/TASK-3 heteromer in the same assay; TREK-1, TREK-2, TASK-2, THIK, TWIK, TRESK; pH dependence; other targets
alternative_actions: paper declares it an open-pore blocker whose apparent IC50 may depend on [K+]; weak native effect up to 400 nM in type-1 cells (mostly TASK-1/TASK-3 heterodimers) suggests low potency on the heteromer (authors, discussion)
neuronal_evidence: Native chemoreceptor cells only (O Donohoe); no neuron in the sources read here

name: PK-THPP
synonyms: compound 23 of Coburn 2012 (declared by the source)
identifier: PubChem CID 53464059 (name match; C29H32N4O2; 1-[1-[6-(4-phenylbenzoyl)-7,8-dihydro-5H-pyrido[4,3-d]pyrimidin-4-yl]piperidin-4-yl]butan-1-one); structure not checked against an opened source; not in the LEGEND catalogue (NOT_FOUND_BY_NAME)
target_composition: TASK-3 (KCNK9) inhibitor; TASK-1 about 10-fold weaker (copied); also inhibits native TASK-1/TASK-3-containing channels
assay: Copied pair (Coburn 2012 via O Donohoe); measured here: HEK-293 TASK-3 cell-attached nPopen; native type-1 cell-attached; Ca2+ imaging
value: copied IC50 35 (TASK-3) and 300 (TASK-1) nM; measured: 85.1 ± 2.6 percent inhibition of TASK-3 at 400 nM (n = 3); native type-1 cells 89 ± 3 percent at 400 nM (n = 10), Ki about 66 nM; [Ca2+]i EC50 45.2 nM
relation: IC50 (copied, ratio about 9); percent inhibition; Ki; EC50 for a Ca2+ response
selectivity_panel_measured: native TASK channel activity in type-1 cells; high-K+ (30 mM) Ca2+ response unaffected at 400 nM; good selectivity over TREK and some other K2P is stated for the compound but from Coburn 2012 (not opened)
not_tested: TASK-1 in the same assay; TREK-1/TREK-2/TRAAK, TASK-2, THIK, TWIK, TRESK; the pH dependence; the heteromer is inferred only
alternative_actions: PK-THPP is a potent inhibitor of the heteromer-rich native channel, so it does not separate TASK-3 from TASK-1/TASK-3 (authors, discussion); other K2P actions only from the copied statement
neuronal_evidence: Yang 2022: 0.1 uM shifted holding current inward by 9.6 ± 2.9 pA in adult rat DMV neurons (n = 5); the authors call it a selective TASK-3 blocker, which is a label not a measurement
role_proposed: comparator (TASK-3 and heteromer; does not separate TASK-1/3)

name: spadin
synonyms: peptide, propeptide-derived (sortilin/NTSR3); 17 residues (not verified against a read source)
identifier: PubChem CID 91826106 (name match; C96H142N26O22); sequence not verified; not in the LEGEND catalogue (NOT_FOUND_BY_NAME)
target_composition: proposed TREK-1 antagonist (earlier report: IC50 about 70 nM at 0 mV after arachidonic-acid pre-activation, copied from Mazella 2010, not opened)
assay: Xenopus oocyte TEVC, mouse TREK-1 (and human TREK-1, Supplement), 21 C, bath 96 NaCl 4 KCl 1 MgCl2 0.3 CaCl2 10 HEPES pH 7.6
value: 1 uM spadin: basal mTREK-1 1.4 ± 0.1 to 1.5 ± 0.1 uA; AA-activated 1.9 ± 0.1 to 2.1 ± 0.1 uA (0 mV); pre-application reduced AA activation by 52.2 ± 14.7 percent
relation: current before and after (no block); percent antagonism of AA activation
selectivity_panel_measured: BL-1249 and DHA activation not antagonised; TREK-2 not blocked and AA activation not antagonised
not_tested: TASK-1, TASK-3, TRAAK, TWIK-1 and the TWIK-1/TREK-1 heteromer in this paper; pH dependence
alternative_actions: binds with high affinity to the neurotensin receptor, which is said to associate with TREK-1 and regulate its surface expression (declared in the introduction of the source); TWIK-1/TREK-1 heterodimer inhibition in astrocytes (title-level hit Q40, not opened)
neuronal_evidence: none in neurons in the sources read here; SCI44 held only a quercetin study where spadin blocked quercetin effect (33908633, not spadin alone) [V5: Labbaf 2025 also reports spadin in mouse reticular thalamic neurons: 1 uM no effect on firing; 10 uM shifted RMP from -65.4 to -53.4 mV (n 9).]
pH_dependence_of_tool: not tested; the test bath was pH 7.6
role_proposed: excluded as a TREK-1 blocker of basal current on the single independent oocyte test; remains a conditional probe of the AA-activation pathway

name: Zn2+ (zinc chloride)
identifier: ChEMBL CHEMBL1200679 (compound_identity.py, NAME_EXACT, record name ZINC CHLORIDE; catalogue id CAT:CHEMBL1200679)
target_composition: TASK-3 (KCNK9) selective block; TASK-1 and TASK-2 virtually unaffected; the TASK-3/TASK-1 concatamer comparatively insensitive
assay: Xenopus oocytes, human TASK-1, -2, -3; native cerebellar granule cell IK(SO)
value: TASK-3 IC50 19.8 at +80 mV; native IK(SO) 0.58 of control at 100 uM
selectivity_panel_measured: TASK-1, TASK-2 (virtually no effect); the concatamer (comparatively insensitive)
not_tested: TREK-1 and other K2P; Kv/Kir/Nav/NMDA actions of Zn2+ (not in the abstract); the pH dependence of the block (H98 and E70 are both required for block, so a pH-dependent block is plausible; INFERENZA, not measured)
alternative_actions: Zn2+ acts broadly (NMDA, GABA-A, Kv and others) outside the abstract read here
neuronal_evidence: Native cerebellar granule IK(SO) reduced to 0.58 of control at 100 uM (abstract)
pH_dependence_of_tool: not stated in the abstract; shared H98 residue makes a pH interaction plausible (INFERENZA)
role_proposed: conditional (a TASK-3 discriminator with a promiscuous cation; abstract-level only)
